claims.text: The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy has a predominantly single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a sharp, large, and hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Sub-critical annealing can induce partial crystallization without causing full phase decomposition or loss of mechanical stability.
Controlled annealing forms refined intergranular boundaries and produces a moderated degree of ordering.
Refined intergranular boundaries and moderated ordering facilitate more reversible domain-wall motion during the magnetostructural transition.
Partial annealing relieves residual internal stresses.
Partial annealing induces controlled crystallite formation.
The annealing-induced microstructure decreases pinning of magnetic domain-wall motion during the transition.
Reduced domain-wall pinning produces a less hysteretic magnetocaloric response.
Reduced domain-wall pinning broadens the magnetocaloric transition while preserving a significant entropy change.
Compared with the as-deposited baseline, controlled annealing will noticeably reduce magnetocaloric hysteresis.
Compared with the as-deposited baseline, controlled annealing will broaden the transition profile.
Controlled annealing will modestly shift the transition temperature.
The annealed material will retain sufficient entropy change for low-field magnetic refrigeration.
The as-deposited alloy has limited heat-exchange rates.
The predicted benefits are restricted to carefully controlled annealing that avoids complete crystallization.
Complete crystallization may cause unwanted phase separation or loss of mechanical properties.
